svg.text: Pressure damage at home: it starts before it is visible
Every pressure ulcer had a first hour, and nobody was looking
The first sign
Redness that does not go white when
you press it, and does not fade on moving
On dark skin, look for a patch that is
darker, purplish, warmer, or firmer than
the skin beside it — and ask about pain
Redness is not always visible. Feel and ask.
Where to look every single day
Sacrum and buttocks — sitting as well as lying
Heels, which lift off the mattress easily
Hips, elbows, shoulder blades, back of head
Ears and nose, under tubing and straps
Under a plaster, a catheter, a wet pad
A chair is not safer than a bed — it is worse
What actually causes it, in order of importance
Unrelieved pressure over a bone — time matters more than weight
Shear: dragging her up the bed instead of lifting, or letting her slide down a chair
Moisture from urine, sweat or a soaked pad, which softens skin so pressure cuts faster
Teaching the family at home
Show them how to look, not just how to turn
Pillows between knees and under calves
Change the wet pad immediately, every time
Give them one thing to report and a number to call
Practices that harm
Rubbing or massaging a red area
Rings and doughnut cushions
Talcum powder, spirit, or hot water
Each was once taught, and each does damage
